name: Mirage superoptimizer and compiler pipeline
scope: Static review of the Mirage checkout at agent_space/mirage (commit f9eb70c254acefc9f3667b2a973d0dcf25471fce, 2026-10-05). It covers the muGraph superoptimizer (src/search: kernel- and threadblock-level enumeration, abstract-expression pruning through egg and Z3, the finite-field probabilistic verifier, and the GeneratorConfig and DimStrategy candidate spaces), the transpiler pass pipeline (resolve_tb_fusion, resolve_tensor_layout with Z3, plan_dtensor_memory and plan_stensor_memory, CUDA/Triton/NKI back ends), and the MPK graph-to-task-graph compiler (python/mirage/mpk/persistent_kernel.py layer methods, src/kernel/annotated_graph.cc, src/kernel/runtime.cc, and the worker event loop in include/mirage/persistent_kernel/persistent_kernel.cuh). The papers are the Mirage OSDI'25 paper (arXiv 2405.05751) and the MPK OSDI'26 paper (arXiv 2512.22219). The MegaBake side is src/megabake/{regions.py, planner.py, schedule.py, memory.py, compiler.py, bodies/gemm.py, bodies/attention.py, bodies/generic.py}, plus SCHEDULER_REUSE.md, ROADMAP.md and the fresh reports in artifacts/full_model_2026-10-18. Questions answered: (1) Can MegaBake use superoptimization or search instead of hand-written region matchers to stay model-generic? (2) Which reuse items in SCHEDULER_REUSE.md are done and which are not? (3) Which Mirage compiler mechanisms map onto MegaBake's measured gaps? No GPU jobs were run.

core_ideas.idea: Multi-level muGraph representation (kernel graph -> threadblock graph -> thread graph)
core_ideas.how_it_works: A kernel graph has DTensors in device memory and operators that are either predefined (matmul or elementwise, which become library calls such as cuBLAS) or KN_CUSTOMIZED_OP. A customized op holds a threadblock graph with an explicit grid_dim, block_dim, forloop_range, per-input imap (which grid axis partitions which tensor dim), fmap (which dim the for-loop iterates) and omap. Threadblock ops act on STensors in shared memory. Accumulator ops (FORLOOP_ACCUM_*) mark the boundary between loop-body and epilogue. The thread level is produced by rule-based fusion, not search. The representation makes tiling, the reduction loop and the cross-op fusion boundary explicit, searchable variables.
core_ideas.where_in_source: agent_space/mirage/include/mirage/kernel, include/mirage/threadblock; search.cc:206-275 creates TB graphs from (grid, block, imap, fmap, frange); persistent_kernel.py:2403-2413 shows MPK reusing the same TBGraph as the task description

core_ideas.idea: Exhaustive bounded enumeration with canonical ordering
core_ideas.how_it_works: DFS adds one operator at a time, at kernel level first and then inside a customized op at threadblock level. check_order requires the new (input_idx, op_type) Order to be strictly greater than the last op's Order, so each DAG is generated once. Depth is limited by max_num_kernel_graph_op=5 and max_num_threadblock_graph_op=9 in the code (the paper says 11), with at most 1 custom TB graph (2 with attention optimization). OpenMP tasks fork below depth 5. The op vocabulary and frange {4,16,64} are fixed in GeneratorConfig.

core_ideas.idea: Abstract-expression pruning (subexpression test via e-graph and SMT)
core_ideas.how_it_works: Each tensor gets a symbolic AbstractExpr (Var, Add, Mul, Div, Pow, Exp, Square, Sqrt, Silu, Gelu, Relu, Clamp, Sum-over-dim). Before an op is added, its output expression is checked against the target program's final expression with subexpr_to_final_expr. This serializes to egg s-expressions and runs an e-graph saturation over the equivalence axioms. Prefixes that cannot be a subexpression are cut. The paper reports RMSNorm search at 11-28 s with pruning, versus 768 s and then over 10 h without it. The axioms omit cancellation, so some equivalent graphs are unreachable by design.

core_ideas.idea: Probabilistic equivalence verification over finite fields
core_ideas.how_it_works: Every operator has a fingerprint() implementation that evaluates it on random inputs in modular arithmetic: values mod P=167, with exponent values mod Q=83, where Q divides P-1, so exp maps into the multiplicative group. Candidate outputs are compared with the reference fingerprints under every output permutation. This is exact for 'Lax' programs (linear ops, division, at most one exp per path). ReLU, clamp and non-polynomial activations are outside the guarantee. Search runs one random test per candidate; a Z3 formal verifier is an alternative. Floating-point rounding and casts are not modeled at all.

core_ideas.idea: Empirical selection: profile every verified muGraph
core_ideas.how_it_works: superoptimize() collects all verified muGraphs, compiles each through the transpiler, times it with CUDA events (profile_iters=1000), and keeps the fastest. No analytical cost model ranks candidates; search only enumerates legal, equivalent candidates. Results are cached in a checkpoint file.

core_ideas.idea: Transpiler pass pipeline (fusion -> layout -> memory -> schedule -> codegen)
core_ideas.how_it_works: resolve_tb_fusion fuses single-consumer elementwise and accumulator chains. resolve_tensor_layout solves a Z3 problem that picks innermost and swizzled dims under copy/MMA constraints with fixed penalty constants. plan_dtensor_memory bump-allocates the global workspace with 128-byte alignment. sched_tb_graph builds pre-loop, loop and post-loop schedules and checks 16-byte copy alignment. plan_stensor_memory does interval allocation of shared memory with first-, best- and worst-fit, keeping the smallest peak. Hopper and Blackwell swizzle planners select layout atoms. Back ends emit CUDA (with Hopper/Blackwell TB variants), Triton or NKI (stubbed in Python).

core_ideas.idea: MPK graph-to-task-graph: most-recent-writer DAG with view-window overlap
core_ideas.how_it_works: Layers are processed in program order. Each read binds to the most recent writer of the same base storage whose bounding box overlaps the read window, which amounts to implicit SSA renaming of reused buffers. Same-rank narrow views get exact boxes. Reshape views fall back to the whole parent, which is conservative. Kahn's algorithm checks for cycles. Residual edges implied by op-level reachability are stripped.

core_ideas.idea: Tensor partitioning and regular event grouping (GCD event grids, fork/join LCM)
core_ideas.how_it_works: Each layer's grid_dim partitions its output. For a producer-consumer edge, event_dim[d] = gcd(producer_partitions[d], consumer_partitions[d]), so one event covers a common tile group and a consumer task waits only on producers overlapping its slice. Fork and join groups are unified by an LCM pass so that every task has one wait event and one trigger event. Graphs where a layer is both join-consumer and fork-consumer (case 2), or both join-producer and fork-producer (case 3), are rejected. Events are linearized so successor tasks are contiguous (first/last index), and a host sanity_check simulates firing. The paper also describes successor- and predecessor-set event fusion and dummy tasks (under 1% overhead).

core_ideas.idea: Device runtime: monotonic event counters, workers plus schedulers, hybrid JIT/AOT
core_ideas.how_it_works: Each task descriptor has a dependent_event and a trigger_event. The worker's thread 0 polls the counter with ld.acquire and __nanosleep(10) until it reaches num_triggers * iteration_num. Because the counters keep counting across invocations, they are never reset. Completion does atom.add.release.gpu, and the last trigger enqueues successors. Per the paper, AOT tasks are pre-enqueued round-robin and JIT tasks (data-dependent attention) are dispatched by scheduler warps. Task descriptors are prefetched into shared memory.

core_ideas.idea: Cross-task pipelining (preload phase plus paged shared memory)
core_ideas.how_it_works: Per the MPK paper, each task is split into a pre-load phase (issue TMA/cp.async) and a compute phase. Shared memory is divided into 32 KB pages (7 per SM on H100 and B200), so task i+1's loads can overlap task i's compute once pages are free. The ablation reports 1.2-1.3x on the final linear of Qwen3-8B on B200. In this checkout the preload identifiers appear only in a few task bodies (ampere/linear.cuh, some Blackwell attention), so the generic paged mechanism could not be located in persistent_kernel.cuh [uncertain].
core_ideas.where_in_source: MPK paper section on cross-task pipelining; include/mirage/persistent_kernel/tasks/ampere/linear.cuh

core_ideas.how_it_works: Each layer method registers a task type plus parameters. TaskRegister generates a variant string and dedups identical ones, then emits a single device switch over registered variants. Parameters are bound at runtime through the task descriptor.

core_ideas.idea: Per-model builders with hand-picked grid sizes (MPK does NOT run the superoptimizer in this checkout)
core_ideas.how_it_works: MPK models (qwen3, dflash, deepseek_v3, glm4_moe, gpt_oss, inkling) call layer APIs with grid_dim chosen by helpers such as grid_for_rmsnorm_linear_layer (96 or 64, with a comment asking whether that covers all Qwen3 models) and _gpl. No file under python/mirage/mpk calls superoptimize or search. The MPK paper says the superoptimizer generates task bodies, but the code ships hand-written CUDA task bodies (tasks/hopper, tasks/blackwell, tasks/cute). In practice MPK is a hand-scheduled, per-model system on top of a generic event runtime.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Fine-grained tile-level dependencies across operator boundaries (MPK GCD events)
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: Between two kernels, a consumer CTA cannot start until the whole producer grid has retired. PDL's cudaGridDependencySynchronize is all-or-nothing per grid, and CUDA Graph edges are per kernel. A megakernel can let consumer tile j start as soon as the gcd-group of producer tiles it reads has signaled, for example the first columns of o_proj output feeding the first RMSNorm rows.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: PDL plus overlapped prologues hides about 2-4 us of launch and ramp per edge but still waits for full producer completion; stream-level concurrency only helps independent branches.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Prefetching the next operator's weights while the current operator drains (MPK cross-task preload; ROADMAP step 9)
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: A kernel cannot issue loads for the next kernel's operands: it does not know their addresses or descriptors, and the next kernel's CTAs do not exist yet. In a persistent kernel a CTA idling at a barrier or event can issue cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 for its next GEMM tiles, keeping HBM busy through the tail.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: PDL lets the next kernel's prologue issue its own prefetches before griddepcontrol.wait, which recovers part of it, but only for one-kernel lookahead, and only when the kernels are PDL-enabled.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Search over fusion boundaries that cross what would be kernel boundaries, with the barrier priced in
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: Mirage's search picks the cheapest muGraph, but its cost is measured per kernel. In a megakernel, the choice to recompute (MegaBake's folding) or fuse norm into a GEMM prologue also removes a grid barrier (~0.7 us plus drain and ramp). A multi-kernel compiler cannot trade 'one extra recompute on every CTA' against 'one global synchronization', because it has no cheap global sync.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: Inductor fuses pointwise into templates (epilogue fusion) but cannot recompute a reduction redundantly in every consumer CTA without a separate kernel.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Single compile-time memory plan over the whole step, including scratch reuse across operators
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: The caching allocator and CUDA Graph pools reuse memory too, but at allocation granularity with no knowledge of which CTA finishes when. A megakernel with known phase lifetimes can alias intermediate workspace tightly (memory.py:574) and keep the working set L2-resident (decode activations are a few KB).
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: CUDA Graph memory pools and Inductor's buffer reuse give comparable footprint. L2 residency across kernels is incidental, not planned.

measured_or_reported_gains: Mirage superoptimizer (arXiv 2405.05751, A100/H100, fp16): up to 3.3x over the best baseline on subgraphs; RMSNorm+MatMul 1.5x (A100) and 1.9x (H100); GatedMLP 1.5x (A100) and 2.7-3.3x (H100); GQA up to 2.2x over hand-written kernels (LLaMA-3-70B shapes, 8K context, TP=4, batch 1); QKNorm up to 1.4x; LoRA 1.1-2.4x; end-to-end PyTorch models 0.9-1.9x. Search time: RMSNorm 11-28 s with pruning versus over 10 h without; up to 4 h for the largest subgraphs. MPK (arXiv 2512.22219, OSDI'26): 1.0-1.7x single-batch serving throughput over SGLang and vLLM on A100, H100 and B200 (64-token prompt, 1024 decode tokens); Qwen3-8B on A100 per-token latency 14.5 ms (vLLM/SGLang) to 12.5 ms (bound about 10 ms); 8xH100 1.1-1.4x; cross-task pipelining 1.2-1.3x on the last linear of Qwen3-8B on B200; compute-communication overlap 1.1x on Qwen3-1.7B on 4xH100. Workers per GPU: 104 (A100), 128 (H100), 144 (B200). [uncertain] whether paper numbers match the current checkout, since code constants differ from the paper (FP_P/FP_Q 167/83 vs 227/113; 9 vs 11 TB ops). MegaBake's own fresh numbers (artifacts/full_model_2026-10-18, H200 MIG 3g.71gb, KV capacity 128, decode kernel_duration_us): SmolLM-135M 1501.8 vs Inductor 1382.1; SmolLM-1.7B 2974.3 vs 2425.0; Qwen2-0.5B 1584.2 vs 1636.0 (MegaBake ahead). Complete calls: 2138 vs 11925 us, 3311 vs 10323 us, and 2380 vs 10739 us.
expected_impact_on_megabake: Ranked by expected decode gain on the 60-SM slice, derived from ROADMAP section 6 breakdowns. (1) MPK-style events in the table launch (step 10), with the GCD grouping only as an encoding optimization. 1.7B decode has about 6 barrier intervals per layer x 24 layers, roughly 150 intervals (267 before folding). Each costs 0.7 us of barrier plus a few us of pipeline drain and ramp at small decode tiles. If events let about half of that tail overlap, saving 2-3 us per interval, the gain is roughly 0.3-0.45 ms of 2.97 ms (10-15%) on 1.7B and a similar absolute amount (0.3-0.4 ms, 20-25%) on 135M. This is the largest structural gain [uncertain: depends on measured per-interval drain, which tools/phase_profile.py can isolate]. (2) Cross-phase weight prefetch (MPK preload, step 9). GEMMs are about 1.9 ms on 1.7B at about 1.8 TB/s versus a ~1.5 ms floor. Hiding the TMA ramp at each of the 169 GEMM starts (about 1-2 us each) gives an estimated 0.15-0.3 ms (5-10%). (3) Search-based config selection for table-launch bodies (dim_strategy-style enumeration plus profiling, which MegaBake already has but disables for full models). The swapAB tile (16/32/64 x 64, 8 stages), split-K, attention chunks and fold limits are each currently one value. Expected 0-10% depending on how far each constant is from optimal on a given model; mostly a generality and robustness gain rather than raw speed on the tested models. (4) Superoptimizer-discovered fusions (RMSNorm into the GEMM prologue, gated MLP into the down-projection prologue). The relevant saving is at most one interval plus one norm per site: about 49 RMSNorms x 2.8 us = 0.14 ms on 1.7B (about 5%), part of which folding already captures. Mirage's reported 1.5-1.9x for RMSNorm+MatMul is for standalone kernels at larger M and will not carry over. (5) Prefill above 64 tokens (3-21x slower than Inductor). The superoptimizer is irrelevant there; the gap is the >64-row GEMM path and the first-generation prefill attention body. Mirage's search could, in principle, propose a FlashAttention-like muGraph (its GQA case), but MPK ships hand-written attention bodies, so the practical path is porting a tuned body family. Summary: search instead of matchers is mainly a generality win (new models compile onto tuned paths), not a decode-speed win; events and prefetch are the speed wins.
generality_and_overfitting_risk: Mirage superoptimizer: model-generic by construction (works on any Lax subgraph), but its candidate spaces are hard-coded. Grid candidates are dim/x with x in 8..256 and 2-D sizes {1024,2048,4096} (dim_strategy.cc:31-75), frange is {4,16,64}, and reduction_dimx is 64 (config.cc). Hardware generality comes only from profiling the survivors on the target GPU. MPK: the runtime is generic, but the compiler front end is per model. Grid choices are hand-picked (grid_for_rmsnorm_linear_layer returns 96 or 64 with a TODO asking whether that covers all Qwen3 models, plus an ad-hoc size//256 workaround for wrong outputs, models/utils.py:3-15; _gpl in dflash/builder.py:65-67). Hopper linear always picks linear_swapAB_hopper (persistent_kernel.py:2438-2442), and RMSNorm registration hard-codes eps 1e-6 (SCHEDULER_REUSE.md section 5). Its 96/64 grids are tuned to 132-SM H100s, not to a 60-SM MIG slice. MegaBake items that look tuned to the tested models or this slice: (a) regions.py:686-720 _rms_norm_chain matches only the HF Llama-style spelling pow -> mean -> add -> rsqrt -> mul; other spellings (x*x, F.rms_norm decompositions, Gemma (1+w)) fall to generic reductions, which stays correct but runs the slower path. (b) regions.py:1250-1263 _attention_head_axes stride heuristic already failed on Gemma 3 single-KV-head (ROADMAP 2.2). (c) bodies/gemm.py:1829-1832 rejects N or K not a multiple of 64 and anything not BF16; models with odd vocab or intermediate sizes or FP16 weights drop to the generic contraction. (d) bodies/gemm.py:1853-1880: table-launch GEMMs get exactly one config ((16|32|64) x 64 tile, 8 stages, one shared smem budget); SWAP_AB_MAX_ROWS=64 and SWAP_AB_ROW_TILES (gemm.py:1893-1896) came from SmolLM and Qwen2 decode on 60 SMs. (e) split-K is off by default because it gave 'no gain on the 60-SM slice' (ROADMAP 6), a decision tied to this SM count; on a 132-SM H100 or a smaller hidden size, the tiles-vs-SMs ratio differs and split-K probably matters. (f) DECODE_MAX_CHUNKS=16 and DECODE_MIN_CHUNK_KEYS=64 (attention.py:422-423), MAP_ELEMENTS_PER_THREAD=4 and _UNROLL_ITERATIONS=16 (generic.py:441,478), and the fold limits _FOLD_MAX_ROUNDS_PER_PHASE=2, _FOLD_MAX_ROUNDS=6 and _FOLD_MAX_PHASES=6 (schedule.py:1381-1384) are untuned constants with no target query. (g) compiler.py:430-431 forces max_plans=1 for full models, so none of the above is re-searched per model or GPU. Generic parts: _worker_count (schedule.py:1364-1384) uses the target SM count and occupancy; the memory planner and dependency derivation are shape-agnostic. How the references avoid overfitting: Mirage enumerates legal candidates and profiles them on the target (kernel.py:596-690); Inductor autotunes templates per shape with a persistent cache; MPK does not avoid it (per-model builders). Recommendation: make each constant in (d)-(f) a small candidate set, prune by legality (divisibility, smem, registers queried from the target), and measure per shape bucket with a persistent cache keyed by (GPU name, SM count, shape). That is Mirage's search-then-profile loop applied to configs instead of graphs.
hardware_portability: Search, abstract-expression pruning, finite-field verification, the dependency DAG, GCD/LCM event grouping and memory planning are target-independent. In Mirage, target specificity enters only through the transpiler's TB code generators (transpiler_tb_hopper.cc, transpiler_tb_blackwell.cc, plan_tb_swizzle_{hopper,blackwell}.cc) and MPK's task variants selected by target_cc (persistent_kernel.py:2427-2447). SM90-specific pieces in MegaBake: the TMA/WGMMA swapAB GEMM (gemm.py rejects anything but sm90a at :1846), TMA descriptors in the device table, and the shared-memory budget (TABLE_GEMM_SHARED_BYTES, gemm.py:1711). Toward SM100: tcgen05 MMA accumulates in TMEM with a 128-row MMA_M (2-CTA 256), so swapAB with a 64-row weight tile does not transfer directly. MPK's SM100 linear tiles 128 output rows (models/utils.py:17-35 split-K comment). Cluster Launch Control could replace static work assignment for JIT-like tasks. Event counters and L2 prefetch (cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2) exist on SM90 and SM100. Toward SM80: no TMA or WGMMA, so cp.async plus mma.sync bodies (MPK ships tasks/ampere/linear.cuh); the event runtime carries over unchanged. To stay target-generic, keep the target query (SM count, smem per block, max active blocks; schedule.py:1364 already does this) as the only source of hardware constants, and express body configs as candidate sets filtered by target capability flags (bodies/blackwell.py is the start). Never derive tile or grid constants from the 60-SM slice.

recommended_actions.action: Add per-phase completion counters to the table launch (ROADMAP step 10). Encode MegaBake's existing exact tile prerequisite sets (schedule.py:816) as counters in the device table, using MPK's monotonic num_triggers * call_index target so nothing is reset. Start with coarse per-phase counters (consumer waits for all producer CTAs of the phases it reads), then add GCD tile groups only where traces show wait time. Keep the grid barrier as fallback for any phase whose prerequisites are not proven.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: 0.3-0.45 ms on 1.7B decode (10-15%) and 0.3-0.4 ms on 135M (20-25%) [uncertain; measure per-interval drain first]
recommended_actions.files_to_touch: src/megabake/schedule.py, src/megabake/codegen.py, src/megabake/runtime.py, src/megabake/memory.py (counter storage), tools/phase_profile.py
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Device table layout with a counter region; host simulation like MPK sanity_check (runtime.cc:970) to prove termination

recommended_actions.action: Turn table-launch constants into searched candidate sets: swapAB row tile, pipeline stages, split-K count, decode attention chunks, fold limits. Re-enable plan search (remove the max_plans=1 override at compiler.py:430-431, or give it a small budget) with per-(GPU, SM count, shape bucket) persistent caching, copying Mirage's 'enumerate legal, verify, profile, keep fastest' loop (kernel.py:596-690).
recommended_actions.expected_gain: 0-10% per model, plus removal of 60-SM-specific tuning (split-K on/off, chunk counts) when moving to other GPUs or models
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Compile time per candidate must stay low (table launches already reuse the compiled kernel across workspace bindings); needs a quiet-clock measurement protocol (ROADMAP 6 clock caveat)

recommended_actions.action: Replace op-spelling matchers with expression-level recognition. Canonicalize each fused scalar or reduction program (regions.py _compose_scalar_chain already builds ScalarExpression trees) into a normal form, with an e-graph (egg via the Python 'egglog' package) or a small rewrite system. Recognize RMSNorm, LayerNorm, SiLU*mul and RoPE by expression, not by aten target sequence. Keep the existing matchers only as fast paths and log every region that falls to a generic body.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: No change on tested models; new models (other RMSNorm spellings, Gemma (1+w), LayerNorm models) reach fused bodies instead of generic paths
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Rules must preserve casts and rounding points (no reassociation of fp32 reductions) to keep the per-region bit-exact contract

recommended_actions.action: Cross-phase L2 weight prefetch (ROADMAP step 9, MPK preload). While a CTA waits on a barrier or counter, issue cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 for its first K-tiles of the next GEMM phase. Addresses are already in the device table.
recommended_actions.prerequisite: None; more effective after events, because events create more waiting slack per CTA

recommended_actions.action: Use a bounded Mirage-style local search only where no tuned body or matcher applies. For a residual subgraph of at most 3-4 ops (e.g. 'x + mean*c + bias with broadcast' from ROADMAP 6 gaps, multi-axis reductions), enumerate fusion groupings and reduction tilings over MegaBake's own primitive families, prune by the finite-field fingerprint on CPU, then verify on GPU against PyTorch. Do not port Mirage's C++ search wholesale: its op vocabulary, Lax restriction and multi-hour worst case do not fit FX graphs with casts.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Coverage of unmatched fusion patterns; small speed effect
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Expression canonicalization (action 3); compile-time budget per region

recommended_actions.action: Fuse RMSNorm into the following GEMM's prologue and the residual add into the GEMM epilogue (Mirage rmsnorm_linear / linear_with_residual) as generic 'reduction-prologue' and 'pointwise-epilogue' hooks in the GEMM body rather than named fusions
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Up to about 0.14 ms on 1.7B (49 norms x 2.8 us), minus what folding already saves; 1-2 barrier intervals per layer
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Bit-exactness of the norm inside the prologue (same fp32 reduction order as the standalone body)
